Many entrepreneurs think they can't afford to waste time on reading books
because they are too busy running their business. They believe that real life
practical experience is much more valuable than the theoretical knowledge
which a book contains , and use this to justify their allergy to books. The
fact is that they aren't good readers, and feel both ashamed and guilty about
this. Trying to create a distinction between theory and practice is very
artificial and short sighted . Books are written by experts , based on their
practical experience . They are willing to share this with you , and it's a
very cost effective way of learning from other people's experiences , because
life is too short to make all your mistakes yourself ! If you are so intent on
implementing your ideas, you may find yourself hurtling down the wrong road at
a 100 mph. You will just end up crashing into a brick wall much faster ! If
reading a book allowed you to identify the fact that there is a better route,
you are likely to be much better off ! Anyone who refuses to read might as
well be illiterate for all practical purposes

Whenever I travel alone, I return with tons of photos, but hardly any of
myself. Because I am so poor at taking selfies, sometimes all I have are pics
of landscape and people, to remember a trip. But it helps to have a pic or two

that particular moment. And that is priceless. I’m often too shy to ask others

though travelling solo, where this lady in her 50s took many photos of me -
most of them posed, but I can’t complain at all. Looking through my photos
today, I found this one. Taken near the river at Ghangaria helipad - the small
village that comes alive for exactly 4 months in a year for pilgrims and

red umbrella, as it poured non stop, and had closed my eyes to capture the

When you have large dataset (> 1 million data point), Machine Learning might
not work go for Deep Learning. If you have seen this note multiple times this
post is for you Do not get misguided by such statements. Many ML algos can
scale to very large dataset or even simple ML algos can be made to run on
decent sized dataset by proper data handling DL might be superior on image and
large text dataset but for tabular traditional ML techniques can be as
perform-ant as any DL technique along with benefits like interpretation, ease
of deployment, low inference time etc Many assume as their experience have
been dealing with limitation of memory dependent libraries like Pandas or
similar in R. Without getting into how Pandas can scale Most modern ML
computing framework can be made to run distributed. Spark ML is one such
library that can scale to very large datasets. Spark also supports XGBoost
that can scale XGBoost computation to 100's of nodes with very less deployment
complexity H2O is another library that can distribute most ML algorithm
Libraries like XGBoost can also be distributed on multiple GPU's to scale on
large dataset There is lot to talk on formats like pyarrow and framework like
RAPIDS, but will stop here hashtag#datascience hashtag#machinelearning
hashtag#xgboost hashtag#h2o hashtag#databricks

Handling Outliers Just assume for now you are given dataset as in image below
with lot other features that can conclusively help determine "Overall" runs
saved. How will you handle second row (Ravindra Jadeja) considering Matches is
one of important feature along with others like past runs saved, fitness
level, fielding position etc Will you treat the second row as a) Outlier and
drop the instance b) Outlier and do some specific treatment, if so what c)
Leave the data as it is and train the model (Assume natural data pattern) d)
Check if it is data/reporting issue e) Check this feature in combination with
other features (multivariate analysis/engineering) f) Reduce the impact of
outlier Coming to Outliers in general, not all outliers typically stand out.
Take in many cases fraudulent transaction might look very genuine. Amplify
this with huge dataset and large features space, making it even more complex
to handle outliers. In some case even seasonality or natural drift might look
as outlier Outlier needs closer look at business and data and can be handled
with options mentioned above depending on the nature of outlier. Dig deeper
into it as much as possible hashtag#datascience hashtag#outliers

The 1% Inventor , 99% entrepreneur While its commonplace knowledge that Thomas
Edison invented the electric bulb by failing 10,000 times, what all happened
next is not: 1\. Edison understood that his inventions would mean nothing "for
him", if he is not able to build a viable business around it. 2\. He founded a
company called Edison General Electric Company to start selling bulbs and his
earlier inventions. 3\. However a competitor named The Thomas-Houston company
heavily funded by an investor Mr.Charles Coffin became more dominant. 4\.
Edison then acquired him, backed by investor Mr.JP Morgan and merged both
companies to form The General Electric Company (GE). 5\. For building
defensibility around his product , he patented an electrical distribution
system which provided a ready made power source to bulbs. 6\. The first home,
blazed with electricity was of his investor JP Morgan with the founder, Edison
himself proudly flipping the switch. 7\. Edison understood that for his vision
to electrify the planet , he would need huge capital and raised further round
of capital from Vanderbilt Family. Point is , It was the entrepreneur and
deal-breaker version of Edison that actually created long term intrinsic value
to the ideas and inventions of Edison , the inventor.

Do you want to get into Data Science? But, hesitating as you’re afraid of
advanced maths? Myth: You can’t do Data Science without being an expert of
Advanced Maths & Statistics. Fact: Advanced Maths & Statistics are neither a
necessary nor a sufficient condition for becoming a good Data Scientist. I
know many people who are not experts in Maths but are implementing Machine
Learning models creating immense value for organisations. At the same time, I
also know people who are experts of Maths & Statistics but have no business
understanding and can’t create production level models. In modern Data
Science, most of the models have been already coded in the form of packages
that you can use directly with few lines of code without knowing the complex
maths behind them. In fact, this simplification is one of the key reasons for
fast growth of Data Science. If you’re a beginner, learn Python and get your
hands dirty with Machine Learning by using courses like the famous Coursera
course by Andrew Ng. Also, focus on learning about your domain, key variables
in your field and how they impact the desired output of your organisation.
Later, to become a better Data Scientist, learn more about Probability,
Statistics, Linear Algebra etc. from Khan Academy or Coursera. All the best!
